Name: Donna Bone
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I learned that my students obtained a deeper understanding because the whole process of reading, writing and discussion are connected. My students understood better during discussion , instead of writing. They also understood and expressed ideas more clearly during the writing portion. Speaking to a group still causes some of my students to be hesitant, and learning there are varied ways to learn helps them overcome some of this hesitance.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
One moment that stands out is when students realized that not all states actually observe Daylight Savings Time. This actually opened another opportunity for researching, writing, and discussion. They are seeing that every topic is not cut and dried, that each topic can open up ways to explore additional ones.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you?
